title: My Grandfather's Quiet Habit of Gratitude
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] My grandfather had a small habit that I only truly noticed after many, many years of watching him.
Narrator: Every single night, right before sleeping, he quietly said thanks for three simple, ordinary things.
Narrator: [warmly] Sometimes it was just warm food on the table, or a car that started without trouble, or a short phone call from family.
Narrator: I once asked him why he did this small habit so faithfully, every single night without exception.
Narrator: [gently] He said, noticing blessings helps me remember that a hard day is not the whole story.
Narrator: I asked if he ever skipped a night, maybe when he was too tired, or too upset about something.
Narrator: [wisely] He smiled and said those were exactly the nights he needed the habit most, not the nights he could skip it.
Narrator: I did not understand him fully back then. I thought gratitude was something you felt only during good times.
Narrator: [sadly] Years later, during a very difficult season of my own life, I remembered his words almost by accident.
Narrator: [struggling] I tried it one night, forcing myself to name three small things despite feeling genuinely hopeless about everything else.
Narrator: It felt strange at first, almost forced, like I was pretending to feel something I clearly did not feel.
Narrator: [surprised] But slowly, night after night, I slowly noticed more good parts of each day, even while my problems remained.
Narrator: [warmly] After he passed away, I started this same quiet habit myself, and I still continue it faithfully every single night now.
Narrator: It's such a small, invisible thing, yet it has helped me notice my ordinary day more carefully.
Narrator: Nobody knows I do this. I've never mentioned it to my friends, and I never plan to, honestly.
Narrator: [peacefully] Righteousness, I have learned, often lives quietly inside these small, honest habits, far from anyone's attention or praise.
